title: Component bundle, templates, JavaScript classes, CSS, and metadata configuration
objectives: Name the required files in an LWC bundle folder and why HTML, JavaScript, and js-meta.xml travel together.
Map camelCase folder names to kebab-case custom element tags and state folder naming rules.
Explain that component CSS is scoped to the component and a parent cannot restyle a child's internals.
Read isExposed, targets, and apiVersion in the configuration file as metadata that decides where the component can be placed.
diagnostic_question: A new UI component will not appear in Lightning App Builder, CSS from the parent paints the child's heading, and a teammate named the folder my-widget. Before you debug org settings, which bundle, template, JavaScript class, CSS, and metadata configuration checks come first?
definition: An LWC lives in a folder under lwc that bundles the HTML template, JavaScript class, CSS stylesheet, and js-meta.xml configuration with the same name. The folder cannot nest another component. CSS in the bundle is scoped to that component; the configuration file is metadata that exposes targets such as App Builder. ([Component Folder](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-folder.html); [XML Configuration File Elements](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/reference-configuration-tags.html))
why_it_matters: Wrong folder names, missing meta.xml, or parent CSS that 'should' restyle a child heading are classic interview and build failures. The bundle is metadata; confusing it with record data, or treating CSS like a global stylesheet, produces UI that works in one playground and fails in App Builder.
sixty_second_explanation: Treat the component folder as one apartment unit on a single hallway (the lwc directory). Every room—HTML template, JavaScript class, CSS, js-meta.xml—must wear the unit's name. You cannot stash another apartment inside this one. Wallpaper (CSS) stays on these walls; the neighbor's heading is not yours to repaint, though you may outline the neighbor's door as one box. The lease (js-meta.xml) says whether the unit is listed in App Builder.
deeper_explanation: Create the bundle folder directly under lwc. Folder and files share the same name, including capitalization. Required for a typical UI component: HTML, JavaScript, and the configuration file. CSS, SVG, extra JS utilities, and tests are additional. You cannot nest a component folder inside another component folder. ([Component Folder](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-folder.html))

Names must begin with a lowercase letter, use alphanumeric or underscore characters, stay unique in the namespace, and must not include whitespace, end with an underscore, contain two consecutive underscores, or contain a hyphen. Camel case folder myComponent maps to markup <c-my-component>. Underscores do not map to hyphens. ([Component Folder](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-folder.html))

Every component must have a JavaScript file. UI classes import LightningElement from lwc, extend it, and export default the class. Class names are PascalCase. The JS file can be at most 1 MB. Allowed named imports from lwc include LightningElement, api, track, and wire. ([Component JavaScript File](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-javascript.html))

One stylesheet in the component folder is applied automatically and is scoped to the component in shadow DOM. A parent can style a child as a single element but cannot reach into the child's internals. Use :host in the child's CSS to style its own host. ID selectors are not supported. ([CSS Stylesheets](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-css.html))

componentName.js-meta.xml holds apiVersion, isExposed, targets, description, and related design tags. If isExposed is false, the component is not exposed in builders. To use it in a builder, set isExposed to true and define at least one target. Beginning in Spring ’25, all components must specify an API version to save changes. ([XML Configuration File Elements](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/reference-configuration-tags.html))

mental_model.analogy: One apartment unit on a single hallway: rooms (HTML template, JavaScript class, CSS, js-meta.xml) share the unit name. You cannot nest another apartment in this unit. CSS wallpaper stays on these walls; the lease on the door is js-meta.xml.
useful_mapping: component folder → one apartment, not nestable
HTML template → furnished rooms the visitor sees
CSS → wallpaper scoped to this unit
js-meta.xml → lease listing whether App Builder can show the unit
camelCase to kebab-case → mailbox label c-my-component
where_it_breaks: Inherited CSS properties such as color can still cross the shadow boundary; not all styles are trapped wallpaper.
Utility JS files may use a different filename than the unit.
The analogy does not encode target XML enumerations or LWS.
A parent styling the child as one box is outlining the door, not entering the rooms.

teach_back_prompt: Walk a teammate through an LWC bundle: required files, why my-widget is an illegal folder name, why parent h1 CSS misses the child heading, and which js-meta.xml flags make the component appear in App Builder.

review_schedule.prompt: List required bundle files and the camelCase to kebab-case mapping.

Two-minute interview: bundle, template, JS class, CSS scope, metadata configuration.

claims.claim: An LWC folder sits directly under lwc, cannot nest another component folder, and its files must share the folder name. Folder names cannot contain a hyphen; camelCase maps to kebab-case markup.
claims.validation: Component Folder naming rules and DX project structure.

claims.claim: Every component has a JavaScript file. UI components export a default class that extends LightningElement. The JS file maximum size is 1 MB. Allowed lwc named imports include LightningElement, api, track, and wire.
A component folder can include one stylesheet, automatically applied and scoped to the component. A parent cannot reach into a child's internals with CSS. ID selectors are not supported.

js-meta.xml is required configuration metadata. isExposed false hides the component from builders; exposing it requires isExposed true and at least one target. Spring ’25 onward, components must specify apiVersion to save changes.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: An LWC bundle is one folder under lwc with matching HTML template, JavaScript class, optional CSS, and js-meta.xml. Names are camelCase in files and kebab-case in markup. CSS is scoped. Meta.xml decides App Builder visibility.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the folder: no nested component folders, no hyphens in the name. UI requires HTML plus a default-export class extending LightningElement. CSS in the bundle does not restyle a child's inner h1; I style the child as one element or use :host on the child. If App Builder hides the component, I check isExposed, targets, and apiVersion—not record data.

terminology.plain: The folder that holds one LWC's HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and configuration.
terminology.precise: A folder directly under lwc whose files share the component name. You cannot nest a component in another component folder.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Aura bundle, which uses a different folder and XML shape.
terminology.boundary: Jest tests and SVG icons are extra files, not this lesson's core.

terminology.precise: Required for UI components; same name as the folder. See LWC-001 for <template> root rules.
Required. UI components: import LightningElement from lwc, export default class PascalCase extends LightningElement. Max 1 MB.
terminology.example: export default class LabWidget extends LightningElement {}
terminology.non_example: An Apex class with the same name.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Additional JS files in the folder that cannot be shared as the public UI export.

terminology.plain: The matching .css file that styles only this component.
terminology.precise: At most one stylesheet in the folder, auto-applied, scoped in shadow DOM. Parent CSS cannot restyle child internals. No ID selectors.
terminology.example: labWidget.css h1 { font-size: large; } affects this template's h1 only.
terminology.non_example: A global static resource expected to restyle a nested child's heading.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: :host, which styles this component's host element from inside.
terminology.boundary: SLDS styling hooks details are LWC-009.

terminology.plain: The configuration file that tells Salesforce where the component may appear.
terminology.precise: Required metadata named componentName.js-meta.xml. Controls apiVersion, isExposed, targets, description, and design properties.
terminology.example: isExposed true with lightning__RecordPage so App Builder can host it.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: package.xml, which is a retrieve/deploy manifest, not component design config.
terminology.boundary: Experience Builder target details are larger than this lesson.

terminology.plain: The switch that lists the component in builders.
terminology.precise: If false, the component is not exposed in builders. To appear, set true and define at least one target.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lightning page assignment, which is still required after the component is exposable.
terminology.boundary: FLS on fields the component shows is not isExposed.

terminology.plain: How the folder name appears in HTML: c-my-component.
terminology.precise: Camel case folder myComponent maps to <c-my-component>. Hyphens are illegal in the folder name. Underscores do not become hyphens.
terminology.non_example: Folder my-component, which violates naming rules.
terminology.boundary: Namespaces other than c are packaging topics.

terminology.plain: The Salesforce API version stamped on the LWC configuration.
terminology.precise: Must be 45.0 or higher. Spring ’25: all components must specify apiVersion to save changes. LDS and base components still use latest regardless of this value.
terminology.non_example: The org's release name alone with no tag.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex class API version, a different metadata file.
terminology.boundary: Locker version is org-level, not this tag.

when_to_use: When you must assemble an LWC component bundle: HTML template, JavaScript class, CSS, and js-meta.xml configuration.
When a folder name with a hyphen fails, and you need camelCase that maps to a kebab-case template tag.
When parent CSS does not restyle a child component heading and you must explain scoped stylesheets.
When Lightning App Builder hides the component and the fix is metadata configuration (isExposed, targets, apiVersion), not record data.
When a teammate tries to nest one component folder inside another component folder.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this bundle lesson as a substitute for the LWC custom-element mental model (LWC-001) or for lwc:if / for:each directives (LWC-003).
Do not treat component CSS scoping as a full SLDS or accessibility lesson (LWC-009).
Do not use js-meta.xml targets to explain Lightning Data Service or Apex data access (LWC-006).
Do not configure production org metadata or real customer pages from this component-bundle lab.
Do not invent extra compiler files that are not in the official bundle table.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable scratch org; synthetic labWidget names only.
starting_state_checks: You can deploy Lightning web components.
steps: Create lwc/labWidget with labWidget.html (<template>), labWidget.js (extends LightningElement, default export), and labWidget.js-meta.xml with apiVersion 67.0, isExposed true, and lightning__AppPage.
Add a nested c-lab-child (or a second simple child bundle) with its own h1 and CSS. Put an h1 { font-size } rule only in the parent CSS and confirm the child heading does not change.
Style the child from child.css using :host or its own h1.
Deploy and confirm the component appears in App Builder; then set isExposed false, redeploy, and confirm it disappears from the palette.
guided_completion: If the folder was lab-widget, rename it.
If App Builder is empty, check isExposed and targets before blaming FLS.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Add labWidget.css that styles lightning-button as a descendant in this template only; explain why a nested child's button is not restyled.
evidence: File listing of labWidget.html, .js, .css, .js-meta.xml with matching names.
Note or screenshot: parent h1 rule does not change child heading; builder visibility follows isExposed.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Delete labWidget and any lab child bundles.
hands_on_lab.limitations: Does not cover Experience Cloud LWR capabilities or SVG icons.

decision_table.signal: Need a visible custom UI element in source.
decision_table.choose: One bundle folder under lwc with HTML template, JavaScript class, and js-meta.xml.
decision_table.not: A nested folder inside another component or a hyphenated folder name.
decision_table.why: Component Folder forbids nesting and hyphens; files share the folder name.

decision_table.signal: Markup should read like a web component tag.
decision_table.choose: camelCase folder myWidget and <c-my-widget> in the parent template.
decision_table.not: Folder my-widget or Aura colon notation.
decision_table.why: Camel case maps to kebab-case; hyphens are illegal in the folder.

decision_table.signal: Parent heading CSS does not change a nested child heading.
decision_table.choose: Scoped child CSS or :host on the child; parent may only style the child as one element.
decision_table.not: Assume CSS is global like a static resource.
decision_table.why: Shadow-scoped stylesheets do not reach into child internals.

decision_table.signal: Component missing from Lightning App Builder.
decision_table.choose: Fix js-meta.xml: apiVersion, isExposed true, and a matching target.
decision_table.not: Create business records hoping the palette updates.
decision_table.why: Configuration metadata, not data, exposes the component to builders.

Do not put secrets in js-meta.xml descriptions.
Avoid ID selectors; runtime may transform id values.

isExposed false and blaming the builder.
Omitting apiVersion after Spring ’25 save rules.

mcqs.prompt: Where must an LWC component folder live?

options.A: Directly under the lwc folder, not nested in another component folder

mcqs.rationale: Save each Lightning web component directly under lwc. You cannot nest a component in another component folder.

distractor_explanations.D: Static resources are not LWC bundles.

mcqs.prompt: Folder myComponent appears in a parent template as which tag?
mcqs.rationale: Camel case folder names map to kebab-case in markup.

distractor_explanations.B: Colon syntax is Aura, not LWC.
distractor_explanations.C: Markup uses kebab-case, not mixed camelCase tags.

mcqs.prompt: Why is a folder named my-widget illegal?

options.A: Folder names cannot contain a hyphen
options.D: Widgets cannot be Lightning web components

mcqs.rationale: Names cannot contain a hyphen. Use camelCase myWidget instead.

distractor_explanations.B: Camel case multi-word names are the supported pattern.
distractor_explanations.C: Names must begin with a lowercase letter.
distractor_explanations.D: The name is illegal because of the hyphen, not the word widget.

mcqs.prompt: What must a UI component JavaScript file do?

options.A: Import LightningElement from lwc and export default a class that extends it
options.B: Export only named functions, never a class
options.C: Import Apex as the default export
options.D: Omit the file if HTML exists

mcqs.rationale: Every component must have a JS file; UI components extend LightningElement as the default export.

distractor_explanations.B: UI components use a default-exported class.
distractor_explanations.C: Apex is not the LWC default export.

mcqs.prompt: What is the documented maximum size of a component JavaScript file?
mcqs.rationale: A component’s JavaScript file can have a maximum file size of 1 MB. HTML files have a separate 128 KB limit.

distractor_explanations.B: 128 KB is the HTML file limit, not JS.
distractor_explanations.C: An Apex method limit, not LWC JS size.

mcqs.prompt: Parent CSS sets h1 to xx-large. A nested child also has h1. What happens?

options.A: The style applies to the parent h1, not the nested child's h1
options.B: Both headings always share the parent rule
options.C: The child heading always becomes xx-large

mcqs.rationale: Styles defined in a parent stylesheet do not reach into a child. A parent can style a child only as a single element.

distractor_explanations.B: Shadow scoping blocks that leak for cascaded selectors like h1.
distractor_explanations.C: Not from the parent's h1 selector.

mcqs.prompt: How should a child style its own host element?

options.A: Use the :host selector in the child's CSS
options.B: Use an ID selector in the parent

mcqs.rationale: A component’s stylesheet can style its own element with :host. ID selectors are not supported.

distractor_explanations.C: Apex does not style the host.
distractor_explanations.D: Configuration XML is not a stylesheet.

mcqs.prompt: If isExposed is false, what is true?

options.A: The component is not exposed in the builders

mcqs.rationale: If isExposed is false, the component isn’t exposed in the builders.

distractor_explanations.B: The class can still exist as source.
distractor_explanations.C: isExposed does not change CSS scoping.

mcqs.prompt: App Builder does not list your LWC. isExposed is true. What else does the configuration guide require?

options.A: At least one <target> such as a Lightning page type
options.C: A hyphen in the folder name

mcqs.rationale: To use the component in a builder, set isExposed true and define at least one target.

distractor_explanations.B: Targets are XML configuration, not an object.
distractor_explanations.C: Hyphens are illegal in folder names.

mcqs.prompt: Which named imports from the lwc module are allowed?

options.B: import lwc from 'lwc' as a default

mcqs.rationale: You can use only those named imports for the lwc module. Default and namespace imports from lwc are invalid.

distractor_explanations.B: Default import of lwc is listed as invalid.
distractor_explanations.C: registerTemplate is not an allowed import.
distractor_explanations.D: Namespace imports from lwc are not allowed.

mcqs.prompt: How do you distinguish bundle configuration from business data?

options.A: js-meta.xml and the HTML/JS/CSS files are metadata; Account rows are data
options.D: There is no metadata in LWC

mcqs.rationale: The bundle and configuration file are metadata you deploy. Records remain business data.

mcqs.prompt: Spring ’25 onward, you cannot save component changes. Which configuration tag is the first check?

options.A: apiVersion must be specified on the component
options.D: The folder must contain a hyphen

mcqs.rationale: Beginning in Spring ’25, all components must specify an API version. Unversioned components must have an apiVersion tag set to save changes.

distractor_explanations.B: masterLabel is not the cited save blocker.
distractor_explanations.C: CSS is optional, not the Spring ’25 save rule.

interview_questions.question: What is in an LWC component bundle?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: One folder under lwc with matching HTML template, JavaScript class, js-meta.xml, and optional CSS. You cannot nest another component folder inside it.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I name required UI files and the naming rules: lowercase start, no hyphen, camelCase to kebab-case. JS must default-export a LightningElement class. CSS is one scoped file. Meta.xml is configuration metadata, not record data. Extra utility JS may use a different filename.
tradeoffs: One CSS file vs extra CSS modules
UI bundle vs API module without HTML
follow_ups: What is the JS size limit?
What imports from lwc are legal?
weak_answer_warnings: Putting components inside each other's folders

interview_questions.question: How do folder names become tags in a parent template?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: camelCase folder myComponent becomes <c-my-component>. Hyphens are illegal in the folder. Underscores do not turn into hyphens.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The HTML standard wants a hyphen in custom element names; Salesforce supplies it via namespace plus kebab-case mapping. I never name the folder my-component. I always close the tag. This is markup metadata, not a record API name.
follow_ups: What if the name ends with an underscore?
Can whitespace appear in the folder?
weak_answer_warnings: Using Aura colon tags for LWC

interview_questions.question: Parent CSS enlarges h1 but the nested child heading stays small. Is CSS broken?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: No. Component CSS is scoped. A parent cannot restyle a child's internals. Style the child from its own CSS or outline it as one element.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I explain shadow-scoped stylesheets with the official parent/child h1 example. I mention :host for the child's own host. I admit inherited properties like color can still cross, so I do not overclaim. I do not use ID selectors.
interview_questions.example: parent.css h1 vs child.html <h1>; only the parent's heading becomes xx-large.
tradeoffs: Child-owned CSS vs parent border on the host
weak_answer_warnings: Calling Salesforce CSS global by default

interview_questions.question: The component deploys but Lightning App Builder does not show it. What do you inspect?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: js-meta.xml: isExposed must be true and there must be at least one matching target. Also confirm apiVersion is set so the component can save.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not create records to 'register' the component. Configuration metadata controls builder visibility. I match lightning__AppPage versus RecordPage to the surface we need. I still check FLS only after the palette lists it and a user cannot see fields.
interview_questions.example: isExposed false → palette empty; flip true plus lightning__AppPage → it appears.
tradeoffs: App page vs record page targets

interview_questions.question: Deploy rejects the component name. What rules do you recite?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Start with lowercase, alphanumeric or underscore, unique in the namespace, no whitespace, no trailing underscore, no double underscore, no hyphen, not nested.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look at the folder, not just the class name. PascalCase belongs on the JS class (LabWidget), camelCase on the folder (labWidget). I check we did not drop a component inside another component folder. HTML and JS must match the folder name.
interview_questions.example: Rename my-widget to myWidget; move nested folders up to lwc/.
tradeoffs: Rename vs wrap in a parent that composes children in HTML

interview_questions.question: The JS file will not save because of an import from lwc. What is illegal?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Default or namespace imports from lwc, and imports such as registerTemplate. Use named imports: LightningElement, api, track, wire.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The Component JavaScript File topic lists invalid import shapes. UI components still need export default class extends LightningElement. If the file exceeds 1 MB I split it. I do not confuse this with Apex imports.
interview_questions.example: import { LightningElement, api } from 'lwc'; not import lwc from 'lwc'.

interview_questions.question: When would you skip CSS in the bundle or skip exposing the component?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Skip CSS when base components and styling hooks are enough. Keep isExposed false for internal child components that parents compose in templates, not App Builder.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Not every bundle should be a builder palette item. A child used only as <c-lab-child> inside a parent template can stay unexposed. A page-level widget needs targets. I still keep js-meta.xml and apiVersion. I do not use parent CSS as a substitute for child-owned styles.
interview_questions.example: labWidget exposed on App Page; labWidgetItem isExposed false, composed in the parent template.

interview_questions.question: Teach the bundle using your apartment analogy, then where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: One unit on the lwc hallway: template, class, CSS wallpaper, js-meta.xml lease. No nested apartments. It breaks because inherited color can still cross, and utility files may not share the unit name.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map required files, kebab-case mailbox labels, scoped wallpaper versus outlining the neighbor's door, and the lease flags isExposed and targets. I state Spring ’25 apiVersion. I refuse generic catalog filler. I separate metadata from records.
interview_questions.example: labWidget apartment with a child unit next door on the same hallway, composed in HTML, not nested on disk.
tradeoffs: Simple analogy vs inherited CSS exception
